name: sortstable
algorithm: Sort n u64 keys in four patterns per round (splitmix64-mixed random keys, reversed, a sawtooth of period 1000, 16 distinct keys), each sorted ascending by the language's std stable sort and checked; rounds times (README.md).

skip.c: no std stable sort in C (qsort is the only std sort, and it is not stable)
skip.mk-wrap: the checksum already uses the wrapping operators; sorting has no arithmetic to wrap

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares libraries, each with its own sort algorithm; the checksum (the weighted sum of each sorted pattern, 0xdead if out of order) checks every result
notes: Stable sorts (B20): mk Slice.SortStable; rust sort (driftsort); zig std.sort.block (in place); go slices.SortStableFunc with cmp.Compare (Go has no stable sort without a comparator); cs Enumerable.Order (LINQ stable sort).
